intro.title: Get to know Don!
intro.text: I was born in Korea, grew up across Asia, and studied and worked in Europe before finding my way into EV charging. Drive through the places, people and choices that shaped the road so far.

stops.title: Born in Korea
stops.text:
I was born in South Korea on 27 October 1991 when my mum was making Kimchi. 

15 days after, our family moved to Hong Kong. Few years after, we moved to Singapore and then back to Korea in 1995

stops.title: Early life in Korea
stops.text: I returned to South Korea and lived until 2002. After 2002 Korea Japan Worldcup, our family moved to Beijing, China

stops.title: Life in China
stops.text:
I lived in China spent most of academic life until 2009. 
In 2006–07, I went to United States, spending time in Montana, and Georgia.

stops.title: Uni-life in Korea
stops.text:
I returned to South Korea in 2010 for study Business at Sungkyunkwan University, sponsored by Samsung. 

My years there included military service, exchanges in Europe and a working holiday in Sweden before I returned to finish my degree.

stops.title: Army Duty in Military Police (Kitchen)
stops.text:
I served in the Military Police, but worked in the kitchen. 
I ordered ingredients, planned menus and handled the accounts while helping feed about 550 people in the troop.

stops.title: Life in Spain > France > Sweden
stops.text:
I returned to university and spent an exchange semester in Alicante. 
I met Rachelle there.
After a semester in Alicante, I went to Paris for another exchange semester. After that, I took a break from university and headed to Sweden.

stops.title: A working holiday in Sweden
stops.text: After Paris, I paused university and took a working holiday in Stockholm. I was working in a Chinese kitchen while Rachelle finished university in Manchester

stops.title: Back to Korea finish my degree
stops.text: When the working holiday ended, I returned to University and finished my Business degree in 2016.

stops.title: My first job in automotive
stops.text: I joined Mercedes-Benz Korea as an intern, working on the E-Class launch and a Salesforce CRM rollout. I then moved into after-sales systems and model launches, representing Aftersales in an EV task force. Seeing EVs up close made me especially curious about charging and how it changes everyday car use.

stops.title: Following my interest in charging
stops.text: Charging was the part of EVs I had become most interested in, so I was lucky to join Tesla’s charging team. I worked on AC charging for homes, workplaces and destination sites, including setting up the home-charging program with installer partners and warranty policies.

stops.title: From one automaker to the wider network
stops.text: At Tesla, I had seen charging from an automaker’s side. At TMAP Mobility, I joined the founding eMSP team to build the service across the wider mobility network—partnering with CPOs and connecting their data to TMAP’s platform.

stops.title: A move to the UK, JLR
stops.text: When Rachelle wanted to move to the UK, I was fortunate to find a role at JLR. I now work with local partners on home charging, public charging across 70 markets in Asia Pacific, the Middle East, Africa and Latin America.
